title: Намёки Ильи и поиски Саши  (Ilya's Hints and Looking for Sasha)

segments.t: Rattled by Ilya's smug remarks in the hallway, Max insists that everything between him and Sasha is fine even as jealousy eats away at him. Returning to the kitchen where Elena Pavlovna is calling orders, Max asks Senya if he has seen Sasha anywhere.
Тогда тебе не о чем беспокоиться.
А что это ты так разволновался?
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Yes. Okay.' In Russian, the idea of 'yes' flows naturally into 'okay' without extra filler words.
Тогда тебе не о чем беспокоиться.
'Then you have nothing to worry about.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'to worry', turning the action back on the subject. Senya answers right away.
'What are you hinting at?' Senya brings out the contrast between 'you' and 'on' in a few short words.
'What do you mean?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'sense' before landing on 'sense'.
А что это ты так разволновался?
'Why are you getting so worked up all of a sudden?' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'to get nervous' places the action in the masculine past tense. Senya answers right away.
'Everything is going great between you two, right?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'by' and finishing on 'fine'.
'I am not worked up at all.' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'am nervous' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Yes, Chef.' Sasha anchors the line on 'yes', while 'chef' completes the thought. Senya answers right away.
'Shrimp and arugula salad.' In Russian, the idea of 'salad' flows naturally into 'arugula' without extra filler words.
'Have you seen Sasha anywhere?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'saw'.
'The day before yesterday, yesterday, and today.' The grammar packs 'the day before yesterday' and 'today' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Senya answers right away.
'I saw Sasha.' In Russian, the idea of 'Sasha' flows naturally into 'saw' without extra filler words.
'And I hope I will see her tomorrow too.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'hope so' before landing on 'I will see'. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
Тогда тебе не о чем беспокоиться.
А что это ты так разволновался?
When you watch Scene 18 of Episode 14, listen out for the exchange around ilya's hints and looking for sasha — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
